units.text: EXT. ABANDONED DRIVE-IN THEATRE - NIGHT
A great white screen, torn at one corner, flaps in the wind.
Rows of rusted speaker posts march across a field of dry weeds.
Beyond the fence, a highway hisses with distant headlights.
Fireflies hang over the lot like lit embers, rising and falling with the breath of the dark.
TARIQ HAMADI, 17, skinny, in a thrift-shop blazer, sits on the hood of a dead pickup truck.
His face is turned to the blank screen.
He holds a Walkman in both hands, the earbuds around his neck.
LUCY BRANCH, 17, strides in from the highway side with a flashlight and a backpack.
She wears her father's oversized denim jacket and combat boots caked with mud.
She stops ten feet from the truck.
You came.
units.name: LUCY

units.text: You said ten.
units.name: TARIQ

units.text: It's ten-fifteen.
units.name: LUCY

units.text: I've been here since nine.
units.name: TARIQ

units.text: She sighs.
Climbs onto the hood beside him, and the truck groans under their weight.
For a time she says nothing.
He doesn't either.
Are you going to ask?
units.name: LUCY

units.text: Ask what?
units.name: TARIQ

units.text: Why I wanted to come here.
units.name: LUCY

units.text: I figured you'd tell me.
units.name: TARIQ

units.text: She smiles at the screen.
Flicks off the flashlight.
The dark folds in around them.
My dad took me here. When I was six.
units.name: LUCY

units.text: It was open then?
units.name: TARIQ

units.text: It was the last summer. They played a movie about a talking horse.
units.name: LUCY

units.text: That sounds terrible.
units.name: TARIQ

units.text: It was perfect.
units.name: LUCY

units.text: A breeze lifts the torn corner of the screen.
It sways like a ghost.
She leans back on her elbows, stares at the stars, her voice quiet and strange.
He left the next fall.
units.name: LUCY

units.text: Tariq turns his head.
He gives her the earbuds without a word.
She puts one in.
He puts the other in his own ear.
The Walkman clicks.
A song begins, fragile and slow.
She closes her eyes.
Her mouth trembles.
He keeps his gaze on the screen, as if an image might appear there if they both waited long enough.
I think I can see the horse.
units.name: TARIQ

units.text: Liar.
units.name: LUCY

units.text: I'm serious.
units.name: TARIQ

units.text: There's no horse.
units.name: LUCY

units.text: There's a little bit of horse.
units.name: TARIQ

units.text: She presses her palm over her eyes and laughs again, a wet, helpless sound that breaks halfway into something else.
He sits very still and lets her.
When she lowers her hand, the tears have cut clean tracks through the dust on her face.
Thanks for coming.
units.name: LUCY

units.text: Thanks for asking.
units.name: TARIQ

units.text: Overhead, a firefly drifts across the empty screen and, for a second, is the brightest thing in the world.
